drug_class: Angiotensin II Receptor Blocker (ARB) combined with a Thiazide Diuretic (water pill)
purpose: This medication is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension). It combines two medicines in one pill to help lower your blood pressure more effectively than either medicine alone. Keeping blood pressure under control helps protect your heart, kidneys, and brain from serious problems.
how_it_works: The olmesartan part works by blocking a natural chemical in your body called angiotensin II, which normally causes your blood vessels to tighten. By blocking it, your blood vessels relax and widen, making it easier for your heart to pump blood. The hydrochlorothiazide part is a gentle water pill that helps your kidneys remove extra salt and fluid from your body, which also helps lower your blood pressure.
common_side_effects: Dizziness, especially when standing up quickly. Feeling lightheaded, tired, or weak. Increased urination from the water pill. Low potassium levels which can cause muscle cramps. Headache or upset stomach. Some people notice dry mouth or increased thirst.
warnings: Do NOT take this medicine if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant — it can seriously harm an unborn baby. Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver problems, diabetes, or low potassium levels. Avoid becoming dehydrated. Do not use potassium supplements unless your doctor tells you to. Call your doctor right away if you have severe stomach pain or ongoing diarrhea, as this medicine rarely can cause a serious gut problem called sprue-like enteropathy.
typical_dosing: Usually taken once a day, with or without food. The typical starting dose is olmesartan 20 mg with hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg once daily. Your doctor may increase your dose over time depending on how well your blood pressure is controlled. Always take it at the same time each day and do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor first.
